name: H206 slotted speed sensor (LM393)
description: Slotted infrared photo-interrupter speed sensor: a WYC-H206 slotted optocoupler (IR LED facing a phototransistor across a ~6 mm slot) feeds an LM393 comparator, giving a digital pulse each time an encoder-wheel spoke passes through the slot. OUT is the LM393 open-collector output with a 10 kOhm pull-up to VCC: HIGH while the slot is blocked, LOW while clear. Runs on 3.3-5 V. Sold as: H206 LM393 speed sensor module (common green 3-pin robot-car encoder board with the black WYC H206 slot sensor, header 5V, GND, OUT), usually bundled with a 20-slot encoder disc.
eli5: Counts the holes of a spinning wheel as they pass through its slot, so your board can work out how fast a motor turns.

pins.name: 5V
pins.description: Supply, 3.3-5 V (pin 1, printed 5V). On a 3.3 V board connect it to 3V3, because OUT is pulled up to this supply.

pins.name: OUT
pins.description: Digital output (pin 3): HIGH when the slot is blocked, LOW when clear; open-collector LM393 output with 10 kOhm pull-up to VCC on the board

supplierQuery: H206 LM393 slotted optocoupler speed sensor module encoder
buildNotes: Header order as printed on the green H206 board: 5V, GND, OUT.
On an ESP32 or Pico power the module from 3V3: OUT has a 10 kOhm pull-up to the module supply, so a 5 V supply puts 5 V on the GPIO.

OUT goes HIGH while a spoke blocks the slot and LOW while it is clear (the OUT LED lights when clear). Count rising edges with an interrupt; one wheel turn gives as many pulses as the disc has slots (20 on the usual disc).
The comparator has no hysteresis on this board, so a slow or partly blocked edge can chatter; if counts look too high, ignore edges closer than a few hundred microseconds.
Mount the encoder disc so it passes through the middle of the slot without rubbing; sunlight shining into the slot can stop it seeing spokes.

driver.code:
# H206 / LM393 slotted (photo-interrupter) speed sensor module, MicroPython driver.
# A WYC-H206 slotted optocoupler (IR LED facing an NPN phototransistor across a ~6 mm slot)
# feeds an LM393 comparator. The LM393 output is open-collector with a 10 kOhm pull-up to VCC
# on the board, so OUT is:
#   HIGH (1) while something blocks the slot (an encoder-wheel spoke)
#   LOW  (0) while the slot is clear (the OUT LED lights)
# Power the module from 3.3 V on a 3.3 V board: OUT is pulled up to VCC.
from machine import Pin
import time


class H206:
    def __init__(self, pin, slots=20, min_us=0):
        """pin: GPIO number (or Pin) wired to OUT. slots: holes in the encoder
        wheel (20 on the usual robot-car disc). min_us: ignore edges closer
        together than this (the LM393 has no hysteresis on this board and can
        chatter on a slow edge; try 200-500 us if counts look too high)."""
        self.pin = Pin(pin, Pin.IN) if isinstance(pin, int) else pin
        self.slots = slots
        self.min_us = min_us
        self._count = 0
        self._last = time.ticks_us()
        self.pin.irq(handler=self._edge, trigger=Pin.IRQ_RISING)

    def _edge(self, pin):
        now = time.ticks_us()
        if self.min_us and time.ticks_diff(now, self._last) < self.min_us:
            return
        self._last = now
        self._count += 1

    def blocked(self):
        """True while something is in the slot (OUT high)."""
        return self.pin.value() == 1

    def count(self):
        """Blocked-edges counted since start or the last reset()."""
        return self._count

    def reset(self):
        self._count = 0

    def rpm(self, window_ms=1000):
        """Count pulses for window_ms and return wheel revolutions per minute."""
        start = self._count
        time.sleep_ms(window_ms)
        pulses = self._count - start
        return pulses * 60000 / (self.slots * window_ms)

example.code:
from h206 import H206
import time

sensor = H206({OUT}, slots=20)
while True:
    print('pulses=%d slot=%s' % (sensor.count(), 'BLOCKED' if sensor.blocked() else 'clear'))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
